title: VibeGraph quality layer: generic skill manifest
description: The structured view of one GENERIC skill (skills/<name>/SKILL.md): direction that is true of a KIND of code rather than of one thread, selected by a predicate over the stack profile and injected after the thread skill. A generic skill is the prose half of a quality dimension: every rule carries its why (M-WHY) and a BINDING to the check, pre-check or envelope fact that stands behind it — or says `judgement`, which may never be cited as enforced. A rule that binds to nothing does not exist. The refusal ledger is REQUIRED: what the source skill said that was not carried, and why, so the review travels with the rule (RUN1 4.3). Derived by scripts/skills_validate.mjs from the skill file; a human enables a skill per project in .vibegraph/skills.json.

name.description: kebab-case; equals the folder name (the local skill-author contract).

description.description: Opens with `Use when` and names the trigger, never the workflow: a description that summarises the steps gets followed INSTEAD of the skill (superpowers writing-skills, adopted). No length cap here: the numeric census forbids one, and the body ceiling in generic_skills.ts is derived from the injection budget.

dimension.description: The quality dimension this skill is the prose half of, or `retry` for the flow skill keyed to the retry task fact.

binds.description: Every binding any rule uses. Consistency with rules[].binding is checked by the validator (a listed binding no rule uses, or a rule binding not listed, is refused).

derivedFrom.description: RUN1 assertion ids the rules trace to. A skill no recovered assertion demanded does not exist (brief C.5).

evidence.description: unvalidated until a paired with/without drill is recorded; then validated WITH the drill cited (if/then below). Advisory either way: a skill never changes gating.

limits.description: What the bound checks do NOT verify, in the skill's own words — the pass's `notFollowed` made readable up front. Never empty: a skill that claims its checks see everything is the claim no static check can make.

refused.description: The refusal ledger: what the source skill(s) said that was not carried, each with its reason.

Binding.description: check:<verb> = a registered verb or grammar rule; precheck:<id> = a pre-check line in orchestration.ts by its RUN1/RUN3 name (no exported ids exist yet, gap G14); envelope:<fact> = a fact the envelope already delivers, which the rule teaches the reader to USE; judgement = irreducibly qualitative, never enforced, never cited as such.

SkillPredicate.description: The quality model's predicate grammar plus the task leaf predicate.ts evaluates (TaskFacts). Defined inline so this schema does not depend on flow_spec's internal names. There is no `always`.
